_FLOW: Pre-registered trials for Ω_t. A trial is written BEFORE its intervention fires. A trial registered afterwards can be fitted to its outcome and is not evidence. Status moves registered → baseline-taken → intervention-fired → measuring → reported, and every transition is dated. Computed by scripts/omega_t.py --did.
why_did: Ω_t alone cannot attribute. If archive-anchored addresses rise while the rest of the surface also rises, the instrument recorded a Google change and not a response to the archive. The difference-in-differences arms exist so a rise can be assigned. Without a field control there is no finding — only a series.

trials.question: Does publishing a canonical surface for a liquidated coinage change erasure at its address, relative to archive addresses without one and to the surface at large?
trials.status: REGISTERED — baseline not yet taken, intervention not yet fired
trials.intervention: operativesemiotics.com and .org go live as the canonical surface for the coinage
trials.intervention_date: PENDING — domains registered 2026-08-15, neither resolves as of registration (HTTP 000)

arm_notes.treated: The address receiving a canonical surface. 1 address; 3 with the quoted and attributed variants.
arm_notes.archive-control: Archive-anchored addresses that do NOT receive a new canonical surface in the window. 36 carry a Google AI Overview baseline. Isolates 'the archive is being erased' from 'this address got a surface'.
arm_notes.field-control: Everything else — coinages and entities with no new surface. Isolates surface drift. IF THIS ARM RISES TOO, THE TRIAL FOUND A GOOGLE CHANGE AND NOTHING ELSE.

treated_t0.note: Captured hours before registration, by chance rather than design. It is the only treated-arm baseline that exists and it cannot be retaken.

baseline.still_needed: A same-week baseline for the archive-control and field-control arms on the SAME surface. Most control baselines are dated 2026-08-13; a two-day gap is tolerable, a two-month gap is not, and several controls are older than that.

prediction.response_model: treated Ω_t rises after the surface goes live — legibility attracts erasure
prediction.attrition_model: treated Ω_t falls — the surface supplies provenance the composition can use
prediction.null: treated Ω_t tracks field-control — the surface is invisible to the composition layer

trials.probe_protocol: Same address string, same surface, signed out, unprimed. Capture verbatim with the source strip and the organic result set. Score PER against a published atom table and populate composed_as — term_returned, scope, binding_relation, organic_presence — at every probe. A probe without composed_as cannot measure Ω_d and the substitution is invisible to Ω_t.
trials.falsification: The response reading fails if field-control rises by a comparable amount, which would make this surface drift. It fails differently if treated and archive-control move together, which would mean the surface is irrelevant and the archive's name is the variable. Both outcomes are publishable and neither is the hypothesis.
known_weaknesses: n=1 in the treated arm. One address cannot carry a difference-in-differences on its own; the result will be a direction, not a rate.
Control baselines are not date-matched to the treated baseline.
PER atom tables are stipulated per entity and not standardised, so cross-arm PER comparison inherits that.
The intervention is not blinded and the operator both publishes the surface and scores the captures.

retrospective_prior._status: RETROSPECTIVE AND CONFOUNDED — NOT THE TRIAL, NOT EVIDENCE FOR IT. Computed from historical pairs after the arms were defined. Recorded because it is the first time the archive-versus-field comparison has been computed at all, and because a prior stated before the trial fires cannot later be quietly adjusted to fit the result.
retrospective_prior.reading: On the single date both arms share, erasure at archive-anchored addresses ROSE while erasure elsewhere FELL. That is the direction the response model predicts and the attrition model does not.
why_it_is_not_a_finding: Arms were defined after the pairs existed. Nothing was pre-registered.
INTERVAL LENGTHS ARE NOT MATCHED. Archive t0 clusters at 2026-07-31 (12 of 22); field t0 scatters across 2026-06-27 to 2026-08-09. A two-week interval and a seven-week interval are not comparable.
n=6 in the field arm at the shared endpoint.
The 2026-08-13 batch was an archive-focused probe run. Archive addresses were probed because they are the archive's; field addresses entered for other reasons. That is selection, not sampling.
PER atom tables are stipulated per entity, so cross-arm PER differences inherit that.
retrospective_prior.what_would_convert_it: A same-day probe of BOTH arms with matched interval lengths, on one surface, with arms fixed in advance. That is what OMT-001 is for.
